q: Our contribution is demonstrating that LLM agents benefit from the same principle, and that product-context retrieval can automate specification generation.
r: Include: controlled feature-level comparison of Claude Code with and without a product-context and spec-generation layer, a context mechanism with a coding agent.

q: This paper reframes issue-memory use as a selective, risk-sensitive control problem rather than a pure top-k retrieval problem.
r: Include: memory (context mechanism) controller for LLM coding agents; group (b) is not narrowed by EC5 or EC6, though evidence is smoke-scale offline replay.

q: distills the heuristics discovered during bootstrap exploration into a persistent, verifiable, agent-consumable .bootstrap contract
r: Include: generates a persistent agent-consumable repository contract (context file) and measures downstream agent cost; group (b).

q: We present CommitDistill, an open-source Python prototype that mines a local git history into typed knowledge units
r: IC1: a deterministic git-history retrieval prototype evaluated by annotators and LLM-as-judge, with no coding agent in the loop.

q: We propose CODESKILL, an LLM-based framework that analyzes coding-agent trajectories across diverse tasks, extracts reusable skills, and maintains an evolving skill bank for software-engineering tasks.
r: Include: learned skill bank (skills as context mechanism) for coding agents; group (b), so EC5 and EC6 do not apply.

q: This paper is a system and feasibility report.
r: Include: project memory layer served to coding agents over MCP with token-cost and latency measures; group (b).

q: We introduce TellOnce, a drop-in personalization layer that turns conversational corrections into persistent, scoped, and revisable behavioral rules
r: Include: turns corrections into persistent rules for coding agents, evaluated on compliance across models; group (b).

q: This paper presents a systematic survey of 133 studies on automated issue resolution from a knowledge-centric perspective.
r: EC6: survey of automated issue resolution (SWE-bench style), always excluded for group (c).

q: Versioned procedural contracts, called Skills, encode reusable operating policy
r: Include: design-and-experience report on production coding agents where Skills encode procedure and a harness bounds actions; group (b), borderline.

q: These findings apply to read-only question answering over repositories that can be indexed in advance
r: EC6: compares search paradigms for repository code question answering, a code-understanding task, not code development.
